Very caring people. Can see why that practice has been around for decades. ***Time to edit previous reviews. Very sad as my family has used this vet since the 1960s at their original location on Loop 410. Dr. Ray and Dr. Ann certainly carried on the great tradition of personal care to our pets that was started by Dr. Ray's father and the original founders of the practice. But as life goes on and we all get older, things change and both of them retired. The practice has been taken over by these corporate people and it's not the same. It's corporate America at its worst. We were not even allowed to talk to an actual doctor the last time we were there. The rude woman who seems to run the counter tells us what we are gonna have done and refuses what we want done when it comes to vaccinations. She's usually up front alone with too much to do at once (typical corporate tactic to save money) though that is not her fault. Finally, after the lack of service on our last visit the details of which I won't post here, we reluctantly decided to switch vets after more than 60 years. Then, we had a hassle over getting  our pet's records sent over forcing us to have to go in person to pick them up. Again, you would think an actual vet would care about losing customers but I'm sure they have enough business to keep the assembly line moving. The conversion of our vet hospitals to corporate America has been sad. Dr. Ann and Dr. Ray, we will always miss you and we appreciate the love and care you gave our pets all these years.

Everyone was super nice and accomodating. We called for a last minute urgent appointment as our regular vet is closed mid week and they were able to get us in. We just adopted a senior Chihuahua who was spayed that day and they ensured she had access to medication to keep her comfortable and gave her a heartworm shot to last a year. They have office kitties so be aware if you have a reactive pet (having time to pet and play with the cat was a benefit for us though).

Prices were reasonable and on par with our normal vet.

We confirmed our appointment before leaving my house, but upon arriving at this "vet," we were told an emergency came in and they could not see my cat (who had been puking for 2 days). They offered no alternative solution and the front desk admin actually mocked how sick my cat was. Extremely rude, unprofessional and condescending. I guess you are better off bursting through their front door claiming it is an emergency than scheduling an appointment. Truly abhorrent and I would recommend any other vet in greater Alamo Heights to this place.

Edit since the owner is lying about what happened: Your team NEVER offered to wait or reschedule. Ever.

I can’t say enough wonderful things about this veterinary clinic! Loop 410 Veterinary Clinic

I took my dog to Loop 410 Veterinary Clinic on 4/22 and had a very disappointing experience over the course of two days. During the first visit, I was told my dog needed bloodwork and X-rays. I initially asked for bloodwork first, but after being told X-rays might speed up the process, I agreed. The vet suspected Cushing’s disease and recommended additional testing for the next day. The total for that first visit was $764.75.

I was then told to drop my dog off the next morning between 7:00–7:30 AM for an 8-hour test, and I was quoted $450. I dropped her off at 7:10 AM and was told the vet would call me. I never received any call all day. When I finally called at 4:45 PM, I was told the last blood draw still had not been done and wouldn’t happen until 6:30 PM. By then, my dog had been there for nearly 10 hours.

When I arrived at 6:30 PM to pick her up, I asked about the promised call from the vet and was told my dog had not even been seen by the vet that day. That made no sense considering I was specifically told the vet would contact me.

To make matters worse, I was then charged $639.97 instead of the quoted $450. When I asked why, I was told the original amount was only a “rough estimate,” which had never been explained to me. I was also told a different test had been run, yet no one contacted me beforehand to explain the change in testing or cost.

The lack of communication, unexpected charges, poor organization, and unwillingness to provide management contact information were extremely frustrating. I understand veterinary medicine can be complex, but customers deserve honesty, updates, and transparency—especially when leaving their pet all day and paying significant amounts of money. I cannot recommend this clinic based on my experience.

My pup was having a very urgent situation, and we decided to rush him to the vet. At first, we went to our primary vet, North Star 410 Animal Hospital. It was when they first opened, and they had no veterinarian there, not sure why you're open with no vet, but anyways, the front desk lady acted so uncaring while my spouse is panicking about our dog's life and hands us a card for an ER.

Luckily, we found Loop 410 Veterinary Hospital, the staff was kind, got us in quickly, answered our questions, and made us feel welcomed, heard, and respected.

I will now be moving to this vet as my primary. If I have to spend money, someone who cares about my pups as they care about theirs is the only place I want to go, no matter how much it costs.

I give this place a solid 5/5, 10/10.

I just hope they will write prescriptions to Chewy should I ever need it for food as my insurance is through Chewy and only covers their rx food 100%. If not, ill probably have to keep looking.

They were able to help my dog who was having an allergic reaction. Considering this was an emergency, I think the price was very reasonable. The emergency exam alone was $149 & with my dogs meds it was a little under $300 total.

The only reason I rate it 4 stars is because even though this was considered an emergency, and I was charged the emergency price, they did not treat it as such at first. The receptionist was a little rude and when I walked in the door she said “I’ll be right with you.” Then my mom, who was with me, walked in slightly behind me and started talking to the receptionist & the receptionist cut my mom off and said in a rude tone “I will be right with you.” Which was off putting because my mom simply did not hear her the first time, since she walked in after me. Then they took him back & we were waiting in the lobby. A vet tech came from the back, while the doctor and receptionist were charting notes, and tried speaking to the doctor and said “we have an emergency…”. But the doctor and receptionist paid the vet tech no mind, and the doctor continued talking to the receptionist while she noted what was being said. They took forever, or what felt like forever, to finish while the vet tech was patiently waiting for the doctor to finish so they can give my dog the medication he needed. My dog face was actively swelling and getting worse & they had us waiting for treatment which stressed me out. Mind you the notes being taken weren’t an emergency, they were figuring out scheduling which I feel could have waiting until after my dog was seen.

Regardless, they were able to help my dog and he is okay. The doctor was also really nice & I appreciate everything he did for my baby.
Always a good experience with my pups 🤍

Vets really are amazing. What ultimately made me switch to another clinic was the constant inability to get refills handled in a timely way—both prescription food and prescription medications that my dog cannot miss.

The last two times, I started the refill process two weeks before we were due to run out. I sent multiple emails and made multiple calls, and each time I was told to expect a 24–48 hour turnaround—then nothing happened unless I followed up again. As a customer, I shouldn’t have to babysit the office to make sure essential prescriptions are processed.

I’ve also been given conflicting explanations, ranging from “we can’t get the vet to sign off” to “we don’t work with Chewy anymore,” and that I need to order through the clinic’s preferred online store, which is more expensive.

It’s really unfortunate, because the veterinarian was thorough during appointments. But anything outside the exam room—especially time-sensitive refills—was consistently frustrating and far more difficult than it should be.

I encountered an exceptional human being at Loop 410 Veterinary Hospital at 3100 Nacogdoches Road near Loop 410.  Her name is Anissa.  Recently, my friend and I had found a hurt wild bird.  We think that perhaps it had flown into a glass window of a building.  We wore vinyl gloves and removed it from the pavement and put it in a more comfortable and safe spot on the ground.  It's eyes were open but it did not resist our handling of it at all, which was concerning to us since it was a wild bird.  We observed it for quite some time from a good distance away to see if it would recover, but it did not seem to be recovering.  We, therefore, called a few veterinary clinics, but they said that they did not take in hurt wild birds, and recommended that we try to take care of it ourselves.  We googled on how to take care of a wild bird, and I was going to take it home and try to revive it.  On our way to my home, i noticed Loop 410 Veterinary Hospital, so we stopped there to see if they could help the little bird.  It is there that we encountered their employee Anissa.  Anissa was so caring and kind!!  You could actually see on her face the joy of being able to help a little creature who needed her help.  She told us that she would be happy to take the little bird, run diagnostic tests on it to find out exactly what the problem was, care for its health needs, and hopefully the little bird would make a full recovery.  I am so grateful to Anissa for her goodness and kindness to us and to the little hurt bird.  Thank you so much Anissa!!  The best asset that any company or organization has is it's exceptional people.  Anissa is truly an exceptional human being.  I hope that Loop 410 Veterinary Hospital acknowledges her exceptionalism and rewards her for it.
Highly competent staff and first rate vets.
